body: You can remove this issue, i can't reproduce what i really want to reproduce =(

Here is the solution:
https://stackblitz.com/edit/angular-hxyrrs?file=src%2Fmain.html,src%2Fmain.ts

I have solve your issue in the above stackblitz link but the way you want to do the problem is not a well practice and good approach to do it.

Question:
1. why you want to use the $any with the two way binding directive? 

If you really want to assign the any to the type-members in angular then just when initilizing the type-member assign the "any" type there but still not recommended to assign that type because it makes occuption memory alot and also reading the code become more complex.

Also do not use the $any type with the ngModel (two way binding) because it is not a valid approach to do that. just simply make the normal property and assign its reference.
`name: string = 'Angular';`
`<input [(ngModel)]="name" />`

@AbobakarSadeeq  I understand that i can't use $any with two way binding and i understand how to solve a problem, but error message should be more clear, because in one case it was completely wrong - "error NG5002: Parser Error: Unexpected token '='", and it's hard to find culprit because compiler reports first place where wrong two-way binding met and further places where it met '=' symbol (correct bindings). I thought that i reproduced that issue, but on my stackblitz error was different:
`Parser Error: Unexpected token '=' at column 12 in [$any(name) =$event] in /~/src/main.ts@11:24` (it works as exptected and doesn't report further '=' symbols as unexpected tokens.

The error is at least better now:
> NG5002: Unsupported expression in a two-way binding

`$any` should work, though. Tagging this as a compiler bug.

issue.body:
Some time ago we narrowed down the expressions we support in two-way bindings, because in most cases any apart from property reads doesn't make sense. This ended up preventing users from using `$any` in the binding since it's considered a function call.

These changes update the validation logic to allow `$any`.

Fixes #51165.
